newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ryanair to start new Dublin to France, Belgium flig.
newsitem.headline: Ryanair to start new Dublin to France, Belgium flig.

text.p: Ireland's airline, Ryanair, said it plans to carry freight on two new Boeing 737-200 passenger services linking France and Belgium with Dublin to be launched later this year.

Ryanair is to launch the low-fare services on May 1 with three daily frequencies linking Beauvais, and Charleroi,situated respectively 50 miles north of Paris and 40 miles south of Brussels, respectively, with the Irish republic's capital.

"The 737-200 offers up to three tonnes of cargo capacity per flight and we expect to make good use of it as we have done on our passenger services between Dublin and the UK," a Dublin-based Ryanair official told Reuters.

Ryanair's freight activties, which are franchised out to Pace Airline Services, centre largely on premium services for small-scale shipments such as computer software and automotive parts, the official said.

"We see some scope for this kind of freight service on these new Continental Europe routes and will probably finalise our plans next week," the official added. -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax 5017
